Hair Services

Hair Styling: What's Available at a Salon

Home / Hair Services / Hair Styling

Styling covers everything that happens to hair after the cut and color are done — the blowouts, updos, and finishing techniques that determine how a style actually looks day to day. It's easy to underestimate how much styling contributes to a finished look; the exact same haircut can read completely differently depending on how it's dried, parted, and finished. This guide covers the styling services you'll commonly find at a salon and a few techniques worth learning for the days in between appointments.

Blowouts

A blowout uses a round brush and dryer to smooth and add volume to hair, typically lasting two to four days depending on hair type and humidity. The technique relies on directing tension and heat section by section, which is part of why a professional blowout tends to look smoother and last longer than a rushed at-home version — the brush work matters as much as the dryer itself. Curly and wavy hair can also be blown out straight, though that result is generally more temporary and reverts faster with any moisture.

Updos

Updos range from simple twisted buns to intricate braided styles, and are a common request for events, interviews, or formal occasions. Most stylists recommend booking an updo trial ahead of a major event — a wedding, for example — so there's time to adjust the style before the day it actually matters. Hair texture, length, and even how recently it was washed all affect how well certain updos hold, so it's worth discussing wash timing with your stylist when booking.

Everyday Styling Tips

  • Apply heat protectant before using hot tools, every time — not just for special occasions.
  • Style hair on the "second day" for more texture and better grip, since freshly washed hair is often too slippery to hold curl or volume well.
  • A light-hold texturizing spray can extend a blowout between washes and add grip for updos.
  • Lower heat settings on tools reduce cumulative damage — most hair doesn't need the highest setting to style effectively.

Matching Styling to Hair Type

Fine hair generally styles best with lightweight products and a focus on root volume, since heavier creams or oils can weigh it down quickly. Thick or coarse hair usually needs more product and more heat to fully dry and smooth, but also holds curl and texture longer once it's set. Curly and coily hair styles differently depending on whether the goal is to enhance the natural curl pattern (typically done with diffusers and curl-specific products) or to temporarily straighten it, which is a heavier, more damage-prone process best not done every day.

How Long Styling Services Take

A standard blowout usually takes 30–45 minutes depending on hair length and thickness. Updos vary more widely — a simple twist might take 20 minutes, while an intricate braided or pinned style for a wedding party can take an hour or more per person. If you're planning styling for a group event, ask your stylist how they'd recommend scheduling multiple people so everyone is ready in time.

Making Styling Last Longer

Between professional appointments, a few habits stretch a style further: sleeping with hair loosely wrapped or in a low bun reduces the friction that flattens curls and volume overnight, and a light mist of dry shampoo at the roots can refresh a blowout without a full rewash. None of these fully replace a professional styling session, but they extend the life of one meaningfully.

Styling Is a Skill Worth Investing In

A great cut can look ordinary with poor styling, and an ordinary cut can look great with good styling. If you've never had a professional blowout, it's worth booking one at least once just to see how your hair can look with the right technique — it often changes how you style at home too.
